items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: In fact, I would liken that to the situation with Paul Whiteman. When Paul Whiteman first brought out his syncosymphony...

ctx.x: played real sweet. And since that was my type of music, why that's all I knew. In fact, that's all I was going to play because I -- for the first years when I was out on the road, I had California in my eye, and I was going back at the drop of a hat. In fact, I left my car on blocks the whole time I was on the road for about 20 years and -- because I didn't care anything about the road, you know. I would go home in a minutes. So, I can see where they thought that was (unintelligible).

In fact, I would liken that to the situation with Paul Whiteman. When Paul Whiteman first brought out his syncosymphony, that was the first time they had ever joined -- had a marriage between two types of music. So, it was the same thing.

So, it was the same thing. Here's this colored jazz playing something sweet, or something concertish, or something like that. I could see where they would resent it because it was new. People resent anything new, see, until they become conscious of it and they think it's great.
